sentences.grammar: A proverb: a crow calling a raven black — both are black birds — means accusing someone of your own fault.

sentences.context: If this highborn Oznak should fall to such the Great Masters will be shamed
sentences.simple: If the highborn hero loses to a slave like Belwas, the Masters are shamed; if he wins, it is a hollow victory.
sentences.grammar: 'Fall to' means 'be defeated by'; 'such' means 'a man like this.'

sentences.context: less he had to see of Cersei the happier he was like to
sentences.simple: The less he saw of Cersei, the happier he was.
sentences.grammar: 'The less X, the happier Y' pattern; old 'was like to be' means 'would be.'

sentences.context: when the king laughs, the court laughs with him
sentences.simple: Everyone laughs when the king laughs, whether the joke is funny or not.
sentences.grammar: A general truth about courts: people flatter the king by laughing at his jokes.

sentences.context: A valiant deed unsung is no less valiant
sentences.simple: A brave act is just as brave even if no song praises it.
sentences.grammar: A balanced maxim: 'unsung' (not sung about) does not make the deed 'less valiant.'

sentences.context: drawn to the hole as the tongue is drawn to a missing tooth
sentences.simple: She couldn't stop touching the empty hole, the way your tongue keeps finding a missing tooth.
sentences.grammar: A simile: her thumb is drawn to the hole irresistibly, like a tongue to a gap.

sentences.context: buys a man's silence for a while, but a well-placed quarrel buys it forever
sentences.simple: Gold can buy silence for a time, but a crossbow bolt buys it forever.
sentences.grammar: A grim balanced maxim: 'a bag of dragons' (gold) against 'a well-placed quarrel' (bolt).

sentences.context: one had to splash it about before he realized he could drink it
sentences.simple: You can show Joffrey something, but he won't understand until you force it on him.
sentences.grammar: Plays on the proverb 'you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.'

sentences.context: is to King's Landing as my brother Tyrion is to Ser Gregor Clegane
sentences.simple: White Harbor is as far below King's Landing in stink as Tyrion is below Gregor in size.
sentences.grammar: An 'X is to Y as A is to B' proportion comparing two gaps: smell and size.

sentences.context: Any cat may stare into a fire and see red mice at play
sentences.simple: Anyone can stare into fire and imagine things — that doesn't mean they truly see the future.
sentences.grammar: A dismissive proverb: seeing shapes in flames proves nothing.

sentences.context: know that a king protects his people, or he is no king at all
sentences.simple: A king who does not protect his people is no king at all.
sentences.grammar: A definition by duty: kingship means protection; without it the title is empty.

sentences.context: We will fight a battle, and then we'll rest. Alive or dead, we'll rest
sentences.simple: Either way — alive or dead — we will finally rest.
sentences.grammar: A bleak parallelism: only two outcomes, and rest comes with both.

sentences.context: When the dead walk, walls and stakes and swords mean nothing
sentences.simple: Once the dead rise, walls and weapons are useless — you cannot fight the dead.
sentences.grammar: A conditional stating a rule: when X happens, Y is useless.

sentences.context: One more arrow, and I'll rest, he told himself, half a hundred times
sentences.simple: Jon survives the night by promising himself rest after just one more arrow — half a hundred times.
sentences.grammar: Repetition as endurance: the same promise ('one more') repeated to keep going.

sentences.context: She was no one's daughter now. She was no one
sentences.simple: Arya feels she has lost every identity — daughter, sister, friend — and is now no one.
sentences.grammar: Repetition of negation ('no one') to show identity erased.

sentences.context: The bitch checks my moves before I make them
sentences.simple: Cersei anticipates Tyrion's every move before he makes it.
sentences.grammar: A chess metaphor: she sees his moves before he plays them.

sentences.context: If the girl can be found she will be found
sentences.simple: Varys will pay 100 stags for news of Sansa, 100 dragons for the girl herself.
sentences.grammar: A bounty: two prices, one for information and one for capture.

sentences.context: How could the Kingslayer belong in such exalted company
sentences.simple: How can Jaime, the Kingslayer, belong among such honored knights?
sentences.grammar: A rhetorical question expressing unworthiness.

sentences.context: I opened the door, and did nothing when the vermin began to crawl inside
sentences.simple: Jaime blames himself — he opened the door to corruption and did nothing as it crept in.
sentences.grammar: A metaphor of guilt: opening the door and letting vermin in.

sentences.context: The Fingers are a lovely place, if you happen to be a stone
sentences.simple: The Fingers are only lovely if you are a rock — dry humor meaning it is a miserable place.
sentences.grammar: A conditional joke: 'if you happen to be X' reverses the compliment.

sentences.context: Inch by inch, yard by yard, the turtle crept closer
sentences.simple: The turtle creeps closer — inch by inch, yard by yard.
sentences.grammar: Repetition of measure phrases to show slow, relentless advance.

sentences.context: none of them would die today
sentences.simple: For one day, at least, none of Jon's men would die.
sentences.grammar: A brief reprieve: the future tense marking a single spared day.

sentences.context: I am guilty of being a dwarf, I confess it
sentences.simple: Tyrion's "confession": his real crime is being born a dwarf — the thing he has been on trial for his whole life.
sentences.grammar: A false confession: short parallel clauses turning the charge into an accusation of the court.

sentences.context: If this was power, why did it taste like tedium
sentences.simple: If this was power, why did it taste so boring?
sentences.grammar: A rhetorical question: power as a flavor — and it tastes like tedium.

sentences.context: Lord Tywin Lannister could cow even the Stranger, it would seem
sentences.simple: Tywin is so commanding he could intimidate even Death (the Stranger).
sentences.grammar: Hyperbole: 'cow' (intimidate) applied to the god of death.

sentences.context: honor means no more than our lives, so long as the realm
sentences.simple: Honor and life mean nothing next to the realm's safety — Qhorin's rule.
sentences.grammar: A comparison of values: honor and life are weighed against the realm — and found lighter.

sentences.context: not the when o' dying that matters, it's the how of it
sentences.simple: It doesn't matter when you die, but how — Ygritte's wisdom.
sentences.grammar: A contrast of 'when' vs 'how': the manner of death outweighs its timing.

sentences.context: knew it ought to make her happy, but somehow she still felt
sentences.simple: Joffrey's death should make Arya happy — but with Robb dead too, it feels empty.
sentences.grammar: A contrast: 'ought to' (expected feeling) vs 'somehow' (actual emptiness).

sentences.context: of panic in the back of her throat. Fear cuts deeper than swords.
sentences.simple: Fear cuts deeper than swords — panic is worse than any blade.
sentences.grammar: A maxim: abstract fear is compared to physical swords — and wins.
